finding.claim: CHECKPOINT_INPUT_IDENTITY_ABI/v1 binds much of the consumed-path and model-visible input surface but does not cryptographically close the forward result into one call identity. Shape plus top-1 token is not an output identity: distinct full-logit tensors and distinct calls can share the same shape and top-1 token. A downstream receipt can therefore not prove from the v1 fields alone that a particular semantic/model result came from the exact bound checkpoint+input call.
finding.scope: SOURCE_CONTRACT_GAP_ONLY; no claim that an actual receipt transplant has occurred
finding.credit_boundary: DO_NOT_PROMOTE MODEL_CALL_CAUSAL_IDENTITY OR DOWNSTREAM NODE_RESULT LINEAGE FROM ABI_V1 ALONE

hypothesis.H1: A cryptographic model_call_identity over exact consumed checkpoint identity, exact renderer/token input identity, exact runtime/source identity and an output tensor/result digest is necessary to prevent output-receipt transplantation and causal-lineage ambiguity.
hypothesis.counterhypothesis: For initial checkpoint eligibility, top-1 plus exact input/checkpoint/runtime metadata is sufficient because full output identity is not reused as downstream evidence.
hypothesis.counterassessment: That narrower eligibility claim may be acceptable only if explicitly scoped. Trigger-2/EntityOS intends downstream model-output -> NODE_RESULT -> J-Space/eval lineage, for which a call-level output binding becomes load-bearing.
hypothesis.cheapest_discriminator: Pure deterministic fixture: construct two synthetic forward outputs with identical shape and top-1 token but different remaining logits. Under v1-like fields they collide at the output-summary level; under the successor output tensor digest/model_call_identity they must differ. Add a second transplant fixture that pairs output B with input/checkpoint envelope A and require rejection.
